subtitle: A 22-kilometer white-sand beach in Broome, Western Australia, where camel trains, a fading nudist tradition, and a foreshore rebuild share the same stretch of sand.
spike_statement: Cable Beach nudists have shared their 'north of the rocks' strip with camel tours since the 1960s; regulars have dwindled to three or four.

levers.photo_tone: Low sun over red pindan cliffs and white sand, camel trains in silhouette, the frame honest about who else is on the beach
